new.n: Big Bend stopping place on the Chippewa pinery road (1870s), kept by Sebe Miles
new.pl: Town of Big Bend, Rusk County (big bend of the main Chippewa)
new.v: Coins, tokens, harness and logging hardware
new.st: A logger's memoir of the 1870s walk from Eau Claire to the pineries puts supper, lodging and breakfast at the Big Bend on the third day, at a stopping place kept by Sebe Miles. The previous stops were the Twelve Mile House and the Lake House on Long Lake (Eau Claire Leader, 29 Jun 1917, p. 3). An 1882 list of log-scaling districts names "the main Chippewa from Big Bend" above the Long Lake and Bob's Creek district (Eau Claire News, 16 Dec 1882, p. 3), which puts Big Bend on the main river in today's Town of Big Bend. The house's section is not known, so the pin is the town centroid.
new.t: Find the old tote road where it meets the river bend on the 1938 aerial or an old topo; stopping places stood by the road at the water. Private land: ask.

new.pl: Connors Lake, Flambeau River State Forest, Sawyer County
new.v: Coins, tokens, uniform buttons, camp junk
new.st: Company 1610 opened state forest camp S-56 at Connors Lake on 23 June 1933, "26 mi W of Phillips". It had more than 300 men and side camps at Park Falls and Loretta, and was closed by 1940 (Price County CCC camp list, rootsweb, via the PC thread's research/ccc-camps.tsv). The pin is the lake (GNIS); the barracks clearing is not placed.
new.t: CCC camps leave a cleared flat with footings, a dump and a flagpole base. Look on the 1938 aerial around the lake. This is state forest land, so check the DNR rules or get a permit before detecting. Flambeau River State Forest: check state forest rules before detecting.

new.n: Sheep Ranch ("Skookum Valley") CCC camp F-4 (Co. 644), 1933
new.pl: Jacob Steiger Road area, east Price County (Phillips post office)
new.v: Coins, tokens, uniform buttons, camp junk
new.st: Company 644 opened forest camp F-4, called Sheep Ranch or "Skookum Valley", on 19 May 1933. The list places it on the Jacob Steiger Road, 4 miles east of the Joseph Loula Sr. homestead (Price County CCC camp list, rootsweb). Jacob Steiger took a federal patent in 1903 on part of sec. 24 T38N R3E, and the pin sits there on the guess that the road ran by his land. The Loula homestead is not yet found, so the spot may be off by miles.
new.t: An F-camp was in the national forest, so the site is probably on Chequamegon-Nicolet land: look only, no digging. Use the 1938 aerial to find the clearing.
